title: Overlockers, Coverstitch & Embroidery Machines UK Guide
description: Overlockers (sergers), coverstitch and embroidery machines explained: what they do, who needs one and what to check before you buy one in the UK.
intro: The specialist machines that give home-sewn clothes a professional finish, and the embroidery machines that personalise them.

image.alt: Embroidery on black cloth with scissors

cardText: Overlockers, coverstitch and embroidery machines: what they do and who needs one.

sections.html: An overlocker stitches, trims and neatens a seam in one pass using three or four threads (some use five). It is the machine that makes home-sewn T-shirts and jersey dresses look shop-bought. Look for differential feed, which stops knits stretching or puckering, and easy lower-looper threading.

Coverstitch machines sew the parallel rows of stitching you see on T-shirt hems, with a chain on the back that stretches. Some machines combine overlock and coverstitch, but switching between modes takes time.

Embroidery machines stitch digitised designs inside a hoop. The maximum hoop size decides how large a design can be, so check it first. Combination sewing-and-embroidery machines save space but tie up one machine for both jobs.
Specialist machines reward a proper demonstration. PK Sewing Machines in Leicester sells domestic overlocker and embroidery equipment, and services them too.

faqs.a: Not to start sewing. A zigzag stitch can finish seams. But if you sew a lot of jersey or want professional finishes, an overlocker saves time.
